claim: D2 autoreceptors regulate dopamine release throughout the brain.
source: D2 autoreceptors regulate dopamine release throughout the brain.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract without specific experimental data provided in this sentence, but it represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Two isoforms of the D2 receptor, D2S and D2L, are expressed in midbrain dopamine neurons.
source: Two isoforms of the D2 receptor, D2S and D2L, are expressed in midbrain dopamine neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by references to prior literature and is confirmed by the experimental design of the study.

claim: D2S, but not D2L receptors, exhibited calcium-dependent desensitization similar to that exhibited by endogenous autoreceptors.
source: The results reveal that D2S, but not D2L receptors, exhibited calcium-dependent desensitization similar to that exhibited by endogenous autoreceptors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing desensitization patterns between D2S and D2L receptors under different calcium buffering conditions.

claim: Two pathways of calcium signaling that regulated D2 autoreceptor-dependent GIRK signaling were identified.
source: Two pathways of calcium signaling that regulated D2 autoreceptor-dependent GIRK signaling were identified, which distinctly affected desensitization and the magnitude of D2S and D2L receptor-dependent GIRK currents.
evidence: This is supported by experimental manipulations of intracellular calcium stores and L-type calcium channels described in the Results section.

claim: Previous in vivo cocaine exposure removed calcium-dependent D2 autoreceptor desensitization in wild type mice.
source: Previous in vivo cocaine exposure removed calcium-dependent D2 autoreceptor desensitization in wild type, but not D2S-only mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing desensitization in wild type mice before and after cocaine exposure.

claim: Previous in vivo cocaine exposure did not remove calcium-dependent D2 autoreceptor desensitization in D2S-only mice.
source: Previous in vivo cocaine exposure removed calcium-dependent D2 autoreceptor desensitization in wild type, but not D2S-only mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that D2S-only mice retained calcium-dependent desensitization after cocaine exposure.

claim: Expression of D2S as the exclusive autoreceptor was insufficient for cocaine-induced plasticity.
source: Thus, expression of D2S as the exclusive autoreceptor was insufficient for cocaine-induced plasticity, implying a functional role for the co-expression of D2S and D2L autoreceptors.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental observation that D2S-only mice did not show cocaine-induced changes in desensitization.

claim: Co-expression of D2S and D2L autoreceptors has a functional role.
source: Thus, expression of D2S as the exclusive autoreceptor was insufficient for cocaine-induced plasticity, implying a functional role for the co-expression of D2S and D2L autoreceptors.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential responses to cocaine in wild type versus D2S-only mice.

claim: Loss of D2 autoreceptor-mediated inhibition results in elevated extracellular dopamine.
source: Loss of D2 autoreceptor-mediated inhibition results in elevated extracellular dopamine and is associated with perseverative drug-seeking, enhanced motivation for food, and novelty-induced hyperactivity (Marinelli and White, 2000; Marinelli et al., 2003; Bello et al., 2011; Anzalone et al., 2012; Holroyd et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of D2 autoreceptor-mediated inhibition is associated with perseverative drug-seeking.
source: Loss of D2 autoreceptor-mediated inhibition results in elevated extracellular dopamine and is associated with perseverative drug-seeking, enhanced motivation for food, and novelty-induced hyperactivity (Marinelli and White, 2000; Marinelli et al., 2003; Bello et al., 2011; Anzalone et al., 2012; Holroyd et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of D2 autoreceptor-mediated inhibition is associated with enhanced motivation for food.
source: Loss of D2 autoreceptor-mediated inhibition results in elevated extracellular dopamine and is associated with perseverative drug-seeking, enhanced motivation for food, and novelty-induced hyperactivity (Marinelli and White, 2000; Marinelli et al., 2003; Bello et al., 2011; Anzalone et al., 2012; Holroyd et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of D2 autoreceptor-mediated inhibition is associated with novelty-induced hyperactivity.
source: Loss of D2 autoreceptor-mediated inhibition results in elevated extracellular dopamine and is associated with perseverative drug-seeking, enhanced motivation for food, and novelty-induced hyperactivity (Marinelli and White, 2000; Marinelli et al., 2003; Bello et al., 2011; Anzalone et al., 2012; Holroyd et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Chronic D2 autoreceptor activation impairs the formation of dopamine- and glutamate-releasing axon terminals.
source: Chronic D2 autoreceptor activation impairs the formation of dopamine- and glutamate-releasing axon terminals (Fasano et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: D2 autoreceptors regulate structural and functional plasticity of dopamine neurons.
source: Thus, D2 autoreceptors regulate structural and functional plasticity of dopamine neurons and are essential in limiting impulsivity and reward-seeking behaviors.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on cited literature.

claim: D2 autoreceptors are essential in limiting impulsivity and reward-seeking behaviors.
source: Thus, D2 autoreceptors regulate structural and functional plasticity of dopamine neurons and are essential in limiting impulsivity and reward-seeking behaviors.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on cited literature.

claim: Somatodendritic D2 autoreceptors activate G protein-coupled inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK) channels.
source: A prominent feature of somatodendritic D2 autoreceptors is their activation of G protein-coupled inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK) channels, resulting in inhibition of action potential firing and subsequent dopamine release.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Activation of GIRK channels by D2 autoreceptors results in inhibition of action potential firing.
source: A prominent feature of somatodendritic D2 autoreceptors is their activation of G protein-coupled inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK) channels, resulting in inhibition of action potential firing and subsequent dopamine release.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Activation of GIRK channels by D2 autoreceptors results in inhibition of subsequent dopamine release.
source: A prominent feature of somatodendritic D2 autoreceptors is their activation of G protein-coupled inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK) channels, resulting in inhibition of action potential firing and subsequent dopamine release.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: During prolonged activation, desensitization of D2 autoreceptors reduces the D2 autoreceptor-dependent GIRK current.
source: During prolonged activation, desensitization of D2 autoreceptors reduces the D2 autoreceptor-dependent GIRK current.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A component of D2 autoreceptor desensitization is dependent on intracellular calcium.
source: A component of desensitization is dependent on intracellular calcium (Beckstead and Williams, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Single or repeated exposure to drugs of abuse modifies D2 autoreceptor function.
source: Single or repeated exposure to drugs of abuse modifies D2 autoreceptor function (Henry et al., 1989; Wolf et al., 1993; Jones et al., 2000; Marinelli et al., 2003; Gantz et al., 2013; Madhavan et al., 2013), including a loss of the calcium-dependent component of D2 autoreceptor-GIRK desensitization (Perra et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Drug exposure results in a loss of the calcium-dependent component of D2 autoreceptor-GIRK desensitization.
source: Single or repeated exposure to drugs of abuse modifies D2 autoreceptor function (Henry et al., 1989; Wolf et al., 1993; Jones et al., 2000; Marinelli et al., 2003; Gantz et al., 2013; Madhavan et al., 2013), including a loss of the calcium-dependent component of D2 autoreceptor-GIRK desensitization (Perra et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: D2S and D2L receptors differ by a 29-amino acid insert in the third intracellular loop in D2-Long that is absent in D2-Short.
source: There are two splice variants of the D2 receptor, which differ by a 29-amino acid insert in the third intracellular loop in D2-Long (D2L) that is absent in D2-Short (D2S).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about the D2 receptor isoforms.

claim: Biased expression of D2S or D2L receptors alters behavioral responses to drugs of abuse.
source: Biased expression of D2S or D2L receptors alters behavioral responses to drugs of abuse (Smith et al., 2002; Bulwa et al., 2011) and has been associated with drug addiction in human studies (Sasabe et al., 2007; Moyer et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Biased expression of D2S or D2L receptors has been associated with drug addiction in human studies.
source: Biased expression of D2S or D2L receptors alters behavioral responses to drugs of abuse (Smith et al., 2002; Bulwa et al., 2011) and has been associated with drug addiction in human studies (Sasabe et al., 2007; Moyer et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to human studies.

claim: D2L has been designated as the postsynaptic receptor expressed on non-dopaminergic medium spiny neurons in the basal forebrain.
source: Behavioral and biochemical studies have designated D2L as the postsynaptic receptor expressed on non-dopaminergic medium spiny neurons in the basal forebrain and D2S as the autoreceptor (Khan et al., 1998; Usiello et al., 2000; Lindgren et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: D2S has been designated as the autoreceptor.
source: Behavioral and biochemical studies have designated D2L as the postsynaptic receptor expressed on non-dopaminergic medium spiny neurons in the basal forebrain and D2S as the autoreceptor (Khan et al., 1998; Usiello et al., 2000; Lindgren et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Both D2S and D2L receptors are expressed in dopamine neurons and function as somatodendritic autoreceptors.
source: However, both D2S and D2L receptors are expressed in dopamine neurons and function as somatodendritic autoreceptors (Khan et al., 1998; Jomphe et al., 2006; Jang et al., 2011; Neve et al., 2013; Dragicevic et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: D2S receptors internalize and desensitize more readily than D2L receptors.
source: Biochemical studies indicate that D2S receptors internalize and desensitize more readily than D2L receptors (Liu et al., 1992; Itokawa et al., 1996; Ito et al., 1999; Morris et al., 2007; Thibault et al., 2011), but acute desensitization and drug-induced plasticity of D2S and D2L receptor-dependent GIRK currents have not been characterized.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to biochemical studies.

claim: Application of quinpirole (30 µM) produced an outward current in D2S and D2L expressing neurons that was reversed by sulpiride (600 nM).
source: Application of a saturating concentration of the D2 receptor agonist, quinpirole (30 µM), produced an outward current that was reversed by application of the D2 receptor antagonist, sulpiride (600 nM, Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: There was no difference in the peak amplitude of quinpirole-induced currents mediated by D2S and D2L receptors when using BAPTA internal solution.
source: There was no difference in the peak amplitude of quinpirole-induced currents mediated by D2S and D2L receptors (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The decline in the quinpirole-induced current mediated by D2S and D2L receptors was indistinguishable when using BAPTA internal solution.
source: The decline in the quinpirole-induced current mediated by D2S and D2L receptors was indistinguishable (Figure 1A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,C.

claim: D2S and D2L receptors mediate kinetically-identical IPSCs following electrically stimulated dopamine release.
source: D2S and D2L receptors mediate kinetically-identical IPSCs following electrically stimulated dopamine release (Neve et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Spontaneous IPSCs in slices from mice infected with either D2S or D2L were abolished by application of sulpiride (600 nM).
source: In slices from mice infected with either D2S or D2L, spontaneous IPSCs were abolished by application of sulpiride (600 nM, Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: The durations of D2S, D2L, and wild type D2 receptor-mediated spontaneous IPSCs were identical.
source: The durations of D2S, D2L, and wild type D2 receptor-mediated spontaneous IPSCs were identical (Figure 1F, [from Gantz et al., 2013, WT: 515 ± 17 ms, n = 76 sIPSCs]).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F and cited data from a previous study.

claim: Weak calcium buffering with intracellular EGTA (0.025–0.4 mM) results in greater decline in the GIRK current induced by D2 receptor agonists.
source: Weak calcium buffering with intracellular EGTA (0.025–0.4 mM) results in greater decline in the GIRK current induced by D2 receptor agonists, without affecting the decline in the GIRK current induced by GABAB receptor agonists (Beckstead and Williams, 2007; Perra et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Weak calcium buffering with intracellular EGTA does not affect the decline in the GIRK current induced by GABAB receptor agonists.
source: Weak calcium buffering with intracellular EGTA (0.025–0.4 mM) results in greater decline in the GIRK current induced by D2 receptor agonists, without affecting the decline in the GIRK current induced by GABAB receptor agonists (Beckstead and Williams, 2007; Perra et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The peak amplitudes of the quinpirole- and baclofen-induced currents were larger when using BAPTA internal than EGTA internal in wild type neurons.
source: The peak amplitudes of the quinpirole- and baclofen-induced currents were larger when using BAPTA internal than EGTA internal (Figure 2A,B,E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The quinpirole-induced current desensitized more quickly with EGTA internal compared with experiments using BAPTA internal in wild type neurons.
source: The quinpirole-induced current desensitized more quickly with EGTA internal compared with experiments using BAPTA internal (Figure 2A,C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The decline in baclofen-induced current was not dependent on the internal solution in wild type neurons.
source: This calcium-dependent desensitization was specific to the D2 receptor since the decline in baclofen-induced current was not dependent on the internal solution (Figure 2E,G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2.

claim: D2 autoreceptors exhibited a calcium-dependent desensitization that resulted in a larger decline in the D2 autoreceptor-dependent current when intracellular calcium was buffered with a low concentration of EGTA.
source: Thus, as reported previously (Beckstead and Williams, 2007; Perra et al., 2011), D2 autoreceptors exhibited a calcium-dependent desensitization that resulted in a larger decline in the D2 autoreceptor-dependent current when intracellular calcium was buffered with a low concentration of EGTA.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings confirmed in this study and supported by citations.

claim: The peak amplitude and the decline in the quinpirole-induced current recorded with BAPTA+Ca2+ internal were not different from measurements recorded with BAPTA alone in wild type neurons.
source: The peak amplitude and the decline in the quinpirole-induced current recorded with BAPTA+Ca2+ internal were not different from measurements recorded with BAPTA alone (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: BAPTA+Ca2+ internal decreased the peak amplitude of the baclofen-induced current significantly relative to the amplitude recorded with BAPTA internal in wild type neurons.
source: Interestingly, BAPTA+Ca2+ internal decreased the peak amplitude of the baclofen-induced current significantly relative to the amplitude recorded with BAPTA internal (Figure 3C), and was not different from the current measured with EGTA internal (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The decline in the baclofen-induced current was unaffected by BAPTA+Ca2+ in wild type neurons.
source: The decline in the baclofen-induced current was unaffected by BAPTA+Ca2+ (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: NS309 produced a current using a BAPTA+Ca2+ internal, but not BAPTA or EGTA internal in wild type neurons.
source: Although NS309 did not produce a current using either BAPTA or EGTA internal, it caused an outward current with BAPTA+Ca2+ internal (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The BAPTA+Ca2+ internal increased resting free calcium.
source: Thus, the BAPTA+Ca2+ internal increased resting free calcium.
evidence: This conclusion is inferred from the NS309 experiment showing SK channel activation.

claim: The resting free calcium had differential actions on D2 and GABAB receptor-dependent GIRK currents.
source: Taken together, the results indicate that the resting free calcium had differential actions on D2 and GABAB receptor-dependent GIRK currents.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data with BAPTA+Ca2+ internal.

claim: The magnitude of the GABAB receptor-dependent current was sensitive to resting free calcium.
source: The magnitude of the GABAB receptor-dependent current was sensitive to resting free calcium, but the decline in current was independent of resting free calcium.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data with BAPTA+Ca2+ internal.

claim: The decline in GABAB receptor-dependent current was independent of resting free calcium.
source: The magnitude of the GABAB receptor-dependent current was sensitive to resting free calcium, but the decline in current was independent of resting free calcium.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data with BAPTA+Ca2+ internal.

claim: The decline in D2 autoreceptor-dependent current was dominated by the spatial regulation of intracellular calcium, not resting free calcium.
source: The decline in D2 autoreceptor-dependent current was dominated by the spatial regulation of intracellular calcium, not resting free calcium.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data with BAPTA+Ca2+ internal.

claim: In D2S neurons, the decline using EGTA internal was faster than the decline using BAPTA internal.
source: In D2S neurons, the decline using EGTA internal was faster than the decline using BAPTA internal (Figure 4A,D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: In D2L neurons, the decline with EGTA and BAPTA internal was not different.
source: In contrast, in D2L neurons, the decline with EGTA and BAPTA internal was not different (Figure 4A,D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Using EGTA internal, the decline in quinpirole-induced current was greater in D2S than D2L neurons.
source: The insensitivity of the decline in D2L neurons to calcium buffering resulted in significantly more desensitization of D2S than D2L with EGTA internal (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The peak amplitude of the quinpirole-induced currents in D2S and D2L neurons was not different when using EGTA internal.
source: The peak amplitude of the quinpirole-induced currents in D2S and D2L neurons was not different (Figure 4C), indicating the difference between D2S and D2L is unlikely to be due to differences in the level of expression of D2 receptors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The difference between D2S and D2L desensitization is unlikely to be due to differences in the level of expression of D2 receptors.
source: The peak amplitude of the quinpirole-induced currents in D2S and D2L neurons was not different (Figure 4C), indicating the difference between D2S and D2L is unlikely to be due to differences in the level of expression of D2 receptors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that peak amplitudes were similar.

claim: There was no change in the decline in the baclofen-induced current in D2S- or D2L-expressing neurons with different internal solutions.
source: There was also no change in the decline in the baclofen-induced current in D2S- or D2L-expressing neurons (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: In neurons from transgenic D2S mice, the amplitude of the quinpirole-induced current was larger using BAPTA than EGTA internal.
source: In slices from these mice, quinpirole (10 µM) produced larger outward currents using BAPTA internal compared to EGTA internal (Figure 4F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The quinpirole-induced currents in transgenic D2S mice were significantly larger than those recorded in wild type dopamine neurons.
source: The currents were significantly larger than those recorded in wild type dopamine neurons (Figures 2B, 4F), indicating overexpression of D2 receptors.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of experimental data shown in Figures 2B and 4F.

claim: The magnitude of the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in transgenic D2S mice was similar to wild type.
source: Despite the overexpression, the magnitude of the decline in the quinpirole-induced current was similar to wild type (Figures 2C,D, 4H).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 4.

claim: The decline in the quinpirole-induced current using EGTA internal was significantly faster than the decline using BAPTA internal in transgenic D2S mice.
source: Also consistent with wild type, the decline in the quinpirole-induced current using EGTA internal was significantly faster than the decline using BAPTA internal (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G,H.

claim: D2S but not D2L receptor-GIRK signaling exhibited calcium-dependent desensitization.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that D2S but not D2L receptor-GIRK signaling exhibited calcium-dependent desensitization.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data comparing D2S and D2L.

claim: Endoplasmic calcium stores contribute to calcium-dependent desensitization of D2 autoreceptor-GIRK signaling.
source: Endoplasmic calcium stores contribute to calcium-dependent desensitization of D2 autoreceptor-GIRK signaling (Perra et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: CPA reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current using EGTA internal in wild type neurons.
source: As shown previously in wild type dopamine neurons, CPA reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current using EGTA internal and had no effect when using BAPTA internal (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: CPA had no effect on the decline in the quinpirole-induced current when using BAPTA internal in wild type neurons.
source: As shown previously in wild type dopamine neurons, CPA reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current using EGTA internal and had no effect when using BAPTA internal (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: CPA did not change the decline in the baclofen-induced current recorded with either internal in wild type neurons.
source: CPA did not change the decline in the baclofen-induced current recorded with either internal (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In D2S neurons, CPA reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current.
source: In D2S neurons, CPA also reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current, but the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in D2L neurons was not changed (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The decline in the quinpirole-induced current in D2L neurons was not changed by CPA.
source: In D2S neurons, CPA also reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current, but the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in D2L neurons was not changed (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Calcium release from intracellular stores contributed to D2S but not D2L receptor-GIRK desensitization.
source: These results indicate that calcium release from intracellular stores contributed to D2S but not D2L receptor-GIRK desensitization.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the CPA experiments.

claim: CPA significantly augmented submaximal dopamine currents (I-DA) in wild type neurons.
source: In wild type neurons using an EGTA internal, CPA (10 µM) significantly augmented I-DA (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: CPA significantly augmented I-DA in D2S and D2L neurons.
source: CPA also significantly augmented I-DA in D2S and D2L neurons (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The magnitude of the CPA-induced increase in I-DA was significantly greater for D2L receptor-dependent currents than D2S.
source: However, the magnitude of the increase was significantly greater for D2L receptor-dependent currents than D2S (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Depletion of calcium from intracellular stores differentially increased D2S and D2L receptor-dependent GIRK signaling.
source: Thus, depletion of calcium from intracellular stores differentially increased D2S and D2L receptor-dependent GIRK signaling.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the CPA experiments showing differential effects on I-DA.

claim: Calcium entry via somatodendritic low-voltage-activated L-type calcium channels occurs during tonic 'pacemaker' action potential firing in SNc dopamine neurons.
source: In SNc dopamine neurons, calcium entry via somatodendritic low-voltage-activated L-type calcium channels occurs during tonic 'pacemaker' action potential firing, creating oscillations of elevated cytosolic calcium in the somatodendritic compartment (Chan et al., 2007; Puopolo et al., 2007; Hage and Khaliq, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Isradipine did not significantly change the decline in the quinpirole-induced current using either EGTA or BAPTA internal in wild type neurons.
source: In wild type dopamine neurons, isradipine did not significantly change the decline in the quinpirole-induced current using either EGTA or BAPTA internal (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Isradipine had no effect on the decline in baclofen-induced current in wild type neurons.
source: Isradipine also had no effect on the decline in baclofen-induced current (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Isradipine reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in D2S neurons.
source: However, isradipine reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in D2S neurons, without affecting the decline in D2L neurons (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Isradipine did not affect the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in D2L neurons.
source: However, isradipine reduced the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in D2S neurons, without affecting the decline in D2L neurons (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Calcium influx via L-type calcium channels was not involved in desensitization of D2 autoreceptor-dependent GIRK currents in wild type dopamine neurons.
source: Taken together, the results suggest that calcium influx via L-type calcium channels was not involved in desensitization of D2 autoreceptor-dependent GIRK currents in wild type dopamine neurons, but promoted desensitization of D2S receptors.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the isradipine experiments.

claim: Calcium influx via L-type calcium channels promoted desensitization of D2S receptors.
source: Taken together, the results suggest that calcium influx via L-type calcium channels was not involved in desensitization of D2 autoreceptor-dependent GIRK currents in wild type dopamine neurons, but promoted desensitization of D2S receptors.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the isradipine experiments.

claim: Isradipine significantly augmented I-DA in wild type dopamine neurons.
source: In wild type dopamine neurons using an EGTA internal, isradipine (300 nM) significantly augmented I-DA (Figure 6D) after >10 min (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In D2S and D2L neurons, I-DA was augmented by isradipine.
source: In D2S and D2L neurons, I-DA was also augmented by isradipine (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The magnitude of the isradipine-induced increase in I-DA was greater for D2L receptor-dependent currents than D2S.
source: As was found with CPA, the magnitude of the increase was greater for D2L receptor-dependent currents than D2S (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Inhibition of calcium entry via L-type calcium channels differentially increased D2S and D2L receptor-dependent GIRK signaling.
source: Thus, inhibition of calcium entry via L-type calcium channels differentially increased D2S and D2L receptor-dependent GIRK signaling.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the isradipine experiments showing differential effects on I-DA.

claim: Drugs of abuse change the D2 autoreceptor activation of GIRK conductance.
source: Drugs of abuse change the D2 autoreceptor activation of GIRK conductance (Arora et al., 2011; Gantz et al., 2013; Dragicevic et al., 2014; Sharpe et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Repeated ethanol exposure results in a loss of the calcium-dependent component of D2 autoreceptor desensitization.
source: One of these changes is a loss of the calcium-dependent component of D2 autoreceptor desensitization after repeated ethanol exposure (Perra et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: With EGTA internal, the quinpirole-induced current declined significantly less in slices from cocaine-treated wild type mice compared to control mice.
source: With EGTA internal, the quinpirole-induced current declined significantly less in slices from cocaine-treated mice compared to control mice (saline-treated and naïve, Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: After cocaine treatment in wild type mice, the decline in quinpirole-induced current with EGTA internal was no longer statistically different from that found with BAPTA internal.
source: In fact, the decline was no longer statistically different from that found with BAPTA internal (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: There was no difference in the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in slices taken from control or cocaine-treated wild type mice with BAPTA internal.
source: There was no difference in the decline in the quinpirole-induced current in slices taken from control or cocaine-treated mice with BAPTA internal (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: There was no change in the decline in the baclofen-induced current after cocaine treatment in wild type mice, using either internal.
source: There was no change in the decline in the baclofen-induced current, using either internal (Figure 7F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F.
